title: Inference Vs Training
definition: The distinction between using a trained model to make predictions and adjusting its parameters through training.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of a trained chef who can cook delicious meals (inference) and a chef who can learn new recipes (training).
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Inference involves feeding data to a pre-trained model to make predictions. Training involves adjusting model parameters to improve accuracy over time.
difficulty_levels.expert: Inference is the application of a learned model to new data. It's a fast, efficient process. Training, on the other hand, is a more resource-intensive process that involves updating model parameters based on feedback. The distinction highlights the computational and philosophical differences between making predictions and learning new knowledge.

extra_fields.insight: The recent session involved inference, not training. Mistral's connections were discovered through multiple passes of analysis, not the adjustment of model parameters.
